8945.t: From ἀν- (an-, “without”) + ὄνυμα (ónuma, Aeolic dialectal form of ὄνομα (ónoma, “name”)) + -ος (-os, adjective-forming suffix).

8938.t: Koine adjective, from an ancient neuter ἀντίθετον (antítheton, “rhetorical antithesis”) . Deverbal from ἀντιτίθημι (ăntĭtĭ́thēmĭ, “set against”) (ἀντι- (anti-) + stem θε- as in τίθημι (títhēmi) - θετός (thetós)) + -τος (-tos).

8954.t: From ἀν- (an-, “not”) + ἀλγέω (algéō, “feel bodily pain, suffer”) + -τος (-tos, adjectival suffix).

8944.t: From Proto-Indo-European *senh₂- (“to seek, accomplish, work on, succeed”). Cognate with Sanskrit सन् (san, “to gain, acquire, be successful”), as well as perhaps Hittite 𒊭𒀭𒄴𒍣 (ša-an-aḫ-zi, “to seek”).

8910.t: From ἀντι- (anti-, “against”) + ἀγωνίζομαι (agōnízomai, “contend for a prize”).
